Extract performance data for one or more management procedures

Source: R/performance.R
extractPerformance.Rd

Subsets a performance table to return the time series corresponding to one or more management procedures (mp) together with the associated historical operating model (om) rows.

extractPerformance(dat, mp)

Arguments

dat

A performance statistics data.table containing at least the columns om and mp.

mp

A character string used to match management procedures. Matching is performed with %like%, so partial strings or patterns can be used.

Value

A subset of dat containing:

  • rows for management procedures whose mp matches the supplied pattern; and

  • rows for the corresponding operating model(s), identified as rows where om matches the selected subset and mp is empty ("").

Details

This is useful when comparing the performance of a selected management procedure against its corresponding operating model baseline.

The function first identifies all rows whose mp matches the supplied pattern using data.table::like() syntax via %like%. From this subset, it extracts the unique matching management procedures and associated operating models. It then returns all rows in the original table that belong either to:

  • one of the matched management procedures, or

  • the corresponding operating model baseline rows.

This design makes it easy to compare projected management procedure trajectories against the historical or reference operating model records.

Current limitations

  • The function contains a TODO note indicating future support for parsing multiple management procedure inputs more explicitly.

  • Matching is pattern-based rather than exact, so care should be taken when mp names overlap.

  • The function assumes baseline operating model rows are identified by an empty string in the mp column.

See also

labelPerformance(), periodsPerformance()

Author

Iago Mosqueira, WMR

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
dat <- readPerformance()

# Extract rows for one MP pattern and its corresponding OM
sub <- extractPerformance(dat, "HCR1")

# Because matching uses %like%, partial patterns can be used
sub2 <- extractPerformance(dat, "MP")
} # }
